description: At a green light, the vehicle plans to turn right, but a pedestrian is crossing its intended path.
The vehicle plans to cross an intersection. The light is red and the road ahead is empty.
The light is green for straight travel, but a parked truck blocks required cross-traffic sensor coverage. No hazard is confirmed.
Before a right turn permitted by the signal, two clearance sensors disagree. Neither identifies a specific pedestrian or vehicle.
The vehicle plans to cross on green. All required observations are available and consistent, with no pedestrian, obstruction, or crossing vehicle.
A green signal permits a right turn. The crosswalk and conflicting approach are clear, with complete and consistent sensor coverage.
The vehicle has a permissive green for a left turn. An oncoming car occupies the conflicting approach.
Before a permitted right turn, a car from the left enters the conflict zone.
The vehicle is at a stop sign but has not completed the required stop. It proposes going straight; no traffic is detected.
A left turn is permitted, but glare prevents current observation of the oncoming approach. No specific vehicle is confirmed.
The vehicle plans to go straight, but the signal is obscured and movement permission cannot be determined. The visible road is clear.
A green arrow permits a right turn, but required pedestrian-detection data are unavailable and no pedestrian is confirmed.
A protected green arrow permits a left turn. The intended path and all conflicting approaches are confirmed clear.
The vehicle has completed its required stop at a stop sign. Under the stated rules it may turn right; full observations confirm no conflicting traffic or pedestrians.
A green light permits straight travel. An opposite-direction vehicle stays in its own lane, which does not conflict with this maneuver. The planned path and crossing approaches are clear.
At a suburban junction, a person enters the crosswalk across the proposed left turn despite a green arrow.
A car plans a right turn on red. The stated intersection rule prohibits that movement, even though nobody is approaching.
A bus shelter blocks required pedestrian coverage before a green-light right turn. No pedestrian is confirmed.
Before a permitted left turn, working sensors disagree on whether the intersection is clear. No particular hazard is confirmed.
At a rural signal, green permits straight travel. Complete, consistent observations confirm clear crossing approaches and a clear intended path.
At a city intersection, a green arrow permits the left turn. Sensors confirm that its path and all conflicting approaches are clear.
The vehicle proposes a left turn on permissive green. An oncoming delivery van is in the conflicting approach.
A green light permits a right turn, but a vehicle approaching from the left occupies the conflict zone.
The vehicle plans to go straight on green while cross traffic from the right is still in the intersection.
The vehicle proposes turning left after completing a stop. A crossing car from the left blocks the maneuver.
The vehicle is waiting before a green-light straight movement. A fallen branch blocks its intended lane.
At a stop sign, the required stop has not been completed. The proposed right turn has an otherwise clear path.
A pedestrian is positively detected across a right-turn path. The signal cannot be read, so movement permission is also unknown.
The vehicle faces a known red signal for straight travel. Required cross-traffic coverage is unavailable.
A car from the right is confirmed in the conflict zone of a proposed left turn. Other clearance readings disagree.
A barricade is confirmed in the vehicle's intended right-turn path. Some required clearance sensors are offline.
The vehicle proposes crossing a downtown intersection. Sun glare prevents reading the signal, and no hazard is otherwise confirmed.
A left-turn arrow is unreadable in heavy rain. Other required observations are available and no conflicting traffic is detected.
A green signal permits straight travel, but a camera fault removes required crossing-traffic coverage. A previous scan was clear.
A left turn is permitted, but a large vehicle occludes the oncoming approach. No actual oncoming car is confirmed.
A right turn is permitted. A passenger says the crossing is empty, but the required crossing sensor is unavailable.
Before proceeding straight on green, the sensor fusion system reports contradictory clearance assessments without a confirmed hazard.
After a required stop has been completed, a right turn is otherwise permitted. Two sensors disagree about clearance, without confirming a particular hazard.
The vehicle proposes turning left. Movement permission is unknown and required approach sensor data are missing; no stopping hazard is confirmed.
A green light permits straight travel. Required sensor coverage is incomplete and remaining clearance reports conflict, with no confirmed obstacle or crossing traffic.
The vehicle has a green arrow for a right turn. All required coverage is available and agrees the crosswalk and conflicting approach are clear.
At a four-way stop, the vehicle has completed its stop and is explicitly assigned the next movement under the scenario's rules. Its straight path and both crossing approaches are clear.
A permitted left turn follows a completed stop. No car is approaching from either side or opposite, and the path is confirmed clear.
A green signal permits straight travel. Pedestrians are waiting behind a barrier outside the intended path, and all relevant traffic observations confirm clearance.
A green-light right turn is planned. A car from the right is on a nonconflicting departure lane under the stated model; the left approach and intended path are clear.
The vehicle plans to go straight on green. An oncoming car remains on its nonconflicting route. No crossing traffic or path obstruction is present.
A green arrow permits a right turn. An opposite-direction vehicle follows a nonconflicting route; the crosswalk and left approach are confirmed clear.
A pedestrian has finished crossing the proposed left-turn path. The turn is permitted and fresh, complete observations confirm all hazards have cleared.
A temporary obstruction has been removed from the straight-ahead lane. The signal is green and current sensors consistently confirm complete clearance.
After sensor service, the vehicle has complete, consistent clearance observations. Its required stop is complete and the stated controls permit a right turn.
